description: Table 1 — a single-panel rendered table titled by the caption as "Chemical composition (wt.%) of the steel grades." It has no axes, plot or scale bar; it is a purely tabular composition listing. The header row gives nine column labels: Steel, C, Al, Mn, Si, Mo, B, Ni and Ti. Five data rows follow, one per steel grade, labelled in bold as S1, S2, S3, S4 and S5. Values are given in wt.% to between two and four decimals; dashes ("–") mark elements not deliberately added. S1: C 0.98, Al 6.00, Mn 0.99, Si 0.33, Mo 0.49, B 0.0036, no Ni or Ti. S2: C 1.10, Al 6.05, Mn 1.03, Si 0.34, Mo 0.51, B 0.0039, no Ni or Ti. S3: C 1.05, Al 8.08, Mn 1.00, Si 0.30, Mo 0.50, B 0.0039, no Ni or Ti. S4: C 0.87, Al 5.76, Mn 0.97, Si 0.30, Mo 0.48, B 0.0026, Ni 0.78, Ti 0.10. S5: C 0.60, Al 3.92, Mn 1.01, Si 0.31, Mo 0.50, no B, Ni 0.78, no Ti. The table is the compositional basis of the study: Al varies 3.92–8.08 wt.% (S3 highest), C 0.60–1.10 wt.%, Mn held near 1 wt.%, Si near 0.3 wt.%, Mo near 0.5 wt.%; B is present only in S1–S4, and Ni/Ti only in S4 and S5 (S5 Ni only).

observations.observation: The table lists chemical compositions in wt.% for five steel grades labelled S1, S2, S3, S4 and S5, with columns C, Al, Mn, Si, Mo, B, Ni and Ti.
Al content ranges from 3.92 wt.% (S5) to 8.08 wt.% (S3), the highest Al level in the table; S1 = 6.00, S2 = 6.05, S4 = 5.76.
C content ranges from 0.60 wt.% (S5) to 1.10 wt.% (S2), with S1 = 0.98, S3 = 1.05 and S4 = 0.87.
Mn is kept close to 1 wt.% in every grade (0.97–1.03 wt.%) and Si close to 0.3 wt.% (0.30–0.34 wt.%).
Mo is present at approximately 0.5 wt.% in all five grades (0.48–0.51 wt.%).
B is listed only for S1, S2, S3 and S4 (0.0036, 0.0039, 0.0039, 0.0026 wt.%), and is marked with a dash (not added) for S5.
Ni (0.78 wt.%) is present only in S4 and S5; a dash marks no Ni addition in S1, S2 and S3.
Ti (0.10 wt.%) is present only in S4; all other grades show a dash for Ti.
The caption states the values are for the steel grades 'S1' to 'S5' and are given in wt.%.
The citing text states that Al is incorporated at levels of 5.8–8 wt.% and Mn limited to 1 wt.% in S1–S4 to stabilize ferrite and accelerate the transformation.
The citing text states that C is held at 0.9–1.0 wt.% to achieve full austenitization without polygonal ferrite, consistent with the C values 0.98 (S1), 1.10 (S2) and 1.05 (S3) in the table.
The citing text describes S5 as a lower-alloying concept containing 0.6 % C and 3.92 % Al, matching the S5 row of the table.
The citing text states Ni content was minimized to 0.78 % in S4 and S5 to avoid the polygonal-ferrite formation risk and because of Ni cost, matching the 0.78 wt.% Ni entries in the table.
The citing text states Ti microalloying was applied in Steel S4, consistent with the 0.10 wt.% Ti entry present only in the S4 row.

subfigures.description: Single rendered table of chemical composition in wt.% for five steel grades S1, S2, S3, S4 and S5, with columns Steel, C, Al, Mn, Si, Mo, B, Ni, Ti; dashes indicate elements not added (Ni, Ti absent in S1–S3; Ni present in S4 and S5; Ti only in S4; B absent in S5).
